topic: Atom-safe critical inference for rare-arm adaptive experiments. Fix binary-arm finite populations with bounded potential outcomes, logged predictable assignment probabilities, deterministic bounded Lipschitz critical intensity and signed-residual profiles with supplied uniform moduli, and an explicit early quadratic-variation envelope. Construct a computable stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli-to-Poisson finite-transfer bound and logged-profile enclosure; use certified profile nets and signed-mark convolution to return confidence intervals with uniform finite-experiment coverage and oracle alpha/radius slack, including atomic laws. Prove that the exact late-ramp pair forces every 95%-honest confidence set to have diameter at least 1/8 with limiting probability at least 0.60710678, while a declared high-hazard subfamily admits robust radius at most 0.442M plus arbitrarily small certification slack. Keep HT distributional limits distinct from all-estimator information bounds. Consumer: Liberali et al.'s GUSTO-1/EUROPA adaptive-randomization analysis, conditional on a prespecified expected-endpoint profile bridge. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A stopped coupling, Bernoulli-to-Poisson comparison, Riemann-grid error, random-residual mark bound, and deterministic log-enclosure contraction were derived. The transfer chain uses a predictable stopping rule, summed propensity-probability errors, a Le Cam Bernoulli-to-Poisson step, and Lipschitz Riemann control. Campbell/isometry bounds control random residual marks and early quadratic variation. Rational profile nets, interval elementary functions, and deterministic threshold monotonicity make calibration effective rather than existential. A selection-safe monotone-threshold lemma handles calibration from the same propensity log. Directed BigInt convolution on a 16-bin envelope certified the two-sign ramp expectation below 0.037934 at radius 13/32, while the common void event tends to 0.70710678; a full signed-mark tail calculation gives 0.049830 at radius 0.442M on the high-hazard family. Checks covered completed-log conditioning, pathwise selection, early exceptional propensities, finite-activity atoms, quantile discontinuities, zero and signed profiles, finite-n normalization, and legal high-hazard membership. The constant-profile law was identified as generalized Dickman rather than a new obstruction, so the proposed contribution is the uniform finite-transfer and profile-adaptive interval theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently implement and prove the end-to-end logged-profile-net convolution certificate, including stopped-coupling and deterministic-threshold error allocation, uniformly over the declared adaptive class. EARLY KILL TEST: Reproduce the exact c=a=1/2, delta=1/4 ramp certificate and preserve both the 0.60710678 diameter lower bound and the 0.442M high-hazard radius; any violation stops the calibration route. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_rarearm_levy_frontier.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior proof obtains uniform concentration from fixed product-Bernoulli factorization and a bounded inverse-propensity score; predictable probabilities of order 1/n invalidate that envelope and conditioning on history removes the independent-coordinate step. The web literature either assumes divergent effective information, changes the estimator to recover Gaussianity, or supplies broad betting-based validity without sharp logged-profile radii. A resolution must replace the Lindeberg/product-measure step with a predictable stopping rule, stopped adaptive-to-Bernoulli coupling, marked-Poisson comparison, and threshold enclosures that preserve discontinuous atoms.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An executable interval map from the completed assignment log and certified profile moduli, accompanied by a uniform finite-n coverage inequality and an explicit additive error budget for stopping, Poisson transfer, Riemann discretization, residual marks, early quadratic variation, convolution, and atomic thresholds.

writing_exemplar.why: Its finite-population-first framing and explicit vanishing-propensity boundary provide the closest motivation for entering the regime where Gaussian calibration fails.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive assignments create design-based dependence -> finite populations and vanishing propensities require new asymptotics -> fast decay defeats normal calibration -> finite-hazard experiments need atom-safe profile-calibrated intervals.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt compound-Poisson Stein equations and coupling bounds to stopped conditionally Bernoulli assignments with discretized real signed marks.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An explicit distributional-distance bound for the marked compound-Poisson approximation translates directly into finite-experiment coverage slack.

method_exemplars.technique: Reuse predictable-logging martingale inversion for nonasymptotic validity, replacing its generic terminal boundary with a certified logged-profile threshold.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It already handles predictable propensities and stopping; the missing component is sharp atom-safe critical-law calibration.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior lower bound controls a fixed independent-Bernoulli experiment through common-support finite-cell mixtures, while the rare-arm adaptive observation includes a history-dependent propensity log. Existing interval-width lower bounds concern i.i.d. bounded observations or regular Gaussian regimes. The missing step is an experiment-level comparison of the complete assignment-propensity-outcome laws that preserves class membership and exploits their shared no-rare-assignment atom. Adaptation creates a second boundary: honesty over the containing late-ramp class can force positive diameter even when a high-hazard subclass permits substantially smaller profile-calibrated radii.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-experiment total-variation or modulus theorem for the complete logged observation whose exact late-ramp specialization forces every 95%-honest confidence set to have diameter at least 1/8 with limiting probability at least 0.60710678, paired with a uniformly honest interval attaining radius at most 0.442M plus certification slack on a declared high-hazard subclass.

writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive policies drive propensities toward zero -> inverse-propensity evidence becomes rare and extreme -> valid intervals widen or truncate -> characterize unavoidable width and the profiles permitting adaptation.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The prior construction relies on an exact finite observation kernel, orbit sets, and null-cell handling. The destination has a continuum of Lipschitz profiles, an approximate stopped compound-Poisson kernel, signed residual marks, and a net index selected from the same log used for calibration. Pointwise profile approximation therefore does not imply coverage after selection, and threshold discontinuities prevent a routine quantile-continuity argument. Selective randomization and betting methods protect different forms of adaptivity but do not provide the required deterministic enclosure. The first changed proof step is to replace exact finite-kernel equality by simultaneous outward-rounded probability and threshold bounds that compose monotonically across selection.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A terminating rational-net and directed-convolution algorithm proving simultaneous 95% coverage for the data-selected interval and an oracle inequality for its radius with explicit profile, transfer, convolution, and atomic-threshold slack, including certification of the 13/32 late-ramp radius and the 0.442M high-hazard radius.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative treats analysis choices made after adaptive data as a selection problem and asks what conditioning restores randomization validity.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive data determine later design or analysis choices -> naive reuse of those data breaks calibration -> selection-aware randomization restores validity -> same-log profile-net choice needs a computable atom-safe analogue.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the selection-event randomization argument, replacing Monte Carlo conditioning with simultaneous deterministic profile and threshold enclosures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both procedures use the adaptive experiment to select their inferential calibration and must protect validity after that selection.

method_exemplars.technique: Use martingale inversion to obtain simultaneous validity across stopping times and a finite family of profile candidates, then sharpen each candidate with certified atomic-law thresholds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its simultaneous-validity machinery can protect selection while the new convolution argument supplies the profile-specific radius.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Liberali et al.'s operating characteristics come from trial-data resampling and modeled expected endpoints, not a uniform randomization-based coverage theorem conditional on the supplied bridge. Delayed outcomes and temporal drift can affect later allocation probabilities, so treating predicted endpoints as fixed observed outcomes changes both the assignment log and the rare-arm law. Existing finite-population theory does not isolate bridge error in the critical atomic regime, while simulation-based inversion imposes a stochastic bandit model. The first missing step is a conditional finite-population experiment that separates randomization, bridge-misspecification, and atomic-calibration errors.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A conditional-on-bridge interval procedure for the GUSTO-1/EUROPA-style binary endpoint contrast with at least 95% finite-experiment coverage over the declared bounded finite-population and logged-assignment class, plus an explicit sensitivity allowance for deviations between supplied and realized endpoint profiles.

writing_exemplar.why: It supplies the destination application's ethical motivation, delayed-endpoint mechanism, GUSTO-1/EUROPA scale, and superior-versus-inferior-arm interval asymmetry.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Real-time allocation can reduce adverse outcomes -> delayed endpoints require expected-endpoint assignments -> adaptation concentrates patients on the apparent superior arm -> conditional inference is needed for the undersampled arm and treatment contrast.

method_exemplars.technique: Specialize its finite-population IPW/AIPW martingale decomposition to the real-time adaptive-randomization log while conditioning on fixed potential outcomes and the prespecified bridge.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the nearest design-based theory for nonexchangeable adaptive experiments and identifies the appropriate causal estimand and source of randomness.

method_exemplars.technique: Use selection-aware randomization conditioning to account for design decisions induced by interim expected endpoints, then replace generic simulation with certified rare-arm convolution where applicable.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The endpoint bridge influences subsequent randomization choices, matching the paper's adaptive design-selection structure.

method_exemplars.technique: Use simulated adaptive trajectories as a diagnostic comparator for the certified convolution law while identifying which simulation assumptions are unnecessary under the design-based theorem.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest recent procedure for inverting a practically relevant nonnormal adaptive-sampling distribution.

literature_map:
1. Hadad et al. (2021, PNAS, arXiv:1911.02768) show that decaying adaptive propensities make IPW laws skewed and heavy-tailed, restoring Gaussian inference through variance stabilization.
2. Bibaut et al. (2021, NeurIPS, arXiv:2106.00418) extend variance-stabilized policy-value inference to contextual bandits, again targeting an asymptotically normal estimator.
3. Zhang, Janson, and Murphy (2020, NeurIPS, arXiv:2002.03217) show that naive OLS can be nonnormal after bandit sampling and recover normality through batching.
4. Bibaut and Kallus (2025, Annual Review, arXiv:2405.01281) organize adaptive inference around stabilization, anytime validity, and direct characterization and inversion of nonnormal laws.
5. Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024, CLeaR, arXiv:2311.18274) give fixed-time and anytime-valid adaptive-experiment inference, with propensity truncation governing both validity and width.
6. Waudby-Smith et al. (2024, ACM/IMS JDS, arXiv:2210.10768) obtain anytime-valid off-policy inference under predictable logging without a global importance-weight bound, but do not target sharp critical-profile width.
7. Li and Zhao (2026, arXiv:2602.21998) provide finite-population IPW/AIPW theory for adaptive experiments with vanishing probabilities and expose failure of normal calibration under faster decay.
8. Hong, Leung, and Li (2020, Econometrics Journal) treat finite-population limited overlap when effective sample size diverges; bounded cumulative rare-arm hazard lies beyond their Gaussian regime.
9. Cho, Bibaut, and Kallus (2025, NeurIPS, arXiv:2506.02881) invert simulated nonnormal adaptive laws with asymptotic guarantees, not uniform finite-population atomic certificates.
10. Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026, JRSSB, arXiv:2405.07026) provide selective randomization inference for adaptive design choices, motivating protection against same-log profile selection.
11. Shekhar and Ramdas (2023, arXiv:2310.01547) derive information-projection lower bounds for bounded-mean interval width, but not for adaptive finite-population void-event experiments.
12. Arratia, Goldstein, and Gordon (1989) and Barbour and Xia (1999) supply Chen-Stein and compound-Poisson bounds that do not directly cover predictable stopping with real signed marks.
13. Bhattacharjee and Goldstein (2019, Bernoulli, arXiv:1706.08192) establish generalized Dickman limits for weighted Bernoulli and Poisson sums, so constant-profile Dickman behavior is not a new obstruction.
14. Liberali et al. (2025, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology) motivate delayed-endpoint real-time adaptive randomization using GUSTO-1/EUROPA resampling, while conditional design-based rare-arm coverage remains open.
